content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Screening visit overloaded with many procedures",
      "quote": "Pulmonary function test",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The screening visit includes a large number of procedures (e.g., pulmonary function test, ECHO/MUGA, ophthalmologic assessments, multiple blood samples) all on Day -28, which may be burdensome for patients and sites.",
      "fix": "Consider spreading some screening assessments over a longer window or moving non-essential ones to baseline."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor tissue sample at progression may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor tissue sample taken at pre- treatment, on-treatment,and at disease progression (optional, only if part of the SoC)",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring a tumor tissue sample at disease progression, even if optional, may be challenging to obtain in practice, especially if the patient is not undergoing a standard-of-care biopsy at that time.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the sample is only collected if clinically indicated and consider making it optional without the SoC condition."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiple blood samples on Cycle 1 Day 1 may be excessive",
      "quote": "Blood sample for plasma biomarker assessment and diagnostic development(eg, ctDNA and blood- based biomarkers) (mandatory)",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "On Cycle 1 Day 1, there are several mandatory blood samples (plasma biomarkers, gene expression, exploratory clinical benefit/safety, PK pre- and post-dose, ADA) which may lead to a high blood volume draw and patient discomfort.",
      "fix": "Consolidate blood draws where possible or reduce the number of mandatory samples on the first treatment day."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs and SpO2 measured at every visit may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Vital signs",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and SpO2 are scheduled at every visit including Cycle 1 Day 8 and Day 15, which may be more frequent than needed and adds to patient burden.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital sign assessments to only visits where dosing occurs or when clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ophthalmologic assessments at screening and end of treatment may be hard to schedule",
      "quote": "Ophthalmologic Assessments",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Ophthalmologic assessments require specialized equipment and personnel, which may not be available at all sites, and scheduling them at both screening and end of treatment could cause delays.",
      "fix": "Allow a longer window for these assessments or consider central reading to reduce site burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Eligibility criteria checked at Cycle 1 Day 1 may be redundant",
      "quote": "Eligibility criteria",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Eligibility criteria are checked at both screening and Cycle 1 Day 1, but since randomization occurs on Cycle 1 Day 1, the second check may be redundant and could be removed to reduce burden.",
      "fix": "Remove the eligibility check on Cycle 1 Day 1 or clarify that it is only for confirmation of continued eligibility."
    },
    {
      "title": "Coagulation and troponin only at screening and end of treatment may miss on-treatment changes",
      "quote": "Coagulation",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Coagulation and troponin are only assessed at screening and end of treatment, which may not capture potential drug-induced changes during the treatment period, especially for a drug with known cardiac and bleeding risks.",
      "fix": "Add interim assessments of troponin and coagulation at key timepoints (e.g., Cycle 2 Day 1) to monitor safety."
    },
    {
      "title": "Survival follow-up contact window may be too tight",
      "quote": "These contacts should generally occur within 7 days of the DCO.",
      "page": 64,
      "section": "8.1.3 Survival Assessments",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring survival contacts within 7 days of the data cutoff may be difficult to achieve, especially if patients are hard to reach, and could lead to missing data.",
      "fix": "Extend the window to 14 days or allow flexibility based on site capabilities."
    }
  ]
}
